claims.statement: The literal weighted Hall graph has an integer flow saturating all positive upper-layer supply on each of the first five stored eligible rank-7 census rows at each order 16, 17, and 18.
claims.scope: Exactly 15 rows: the first five eligible rows in stored order from the supplied order-16, order-17, and order-18 p=7 results. For each tree, F is its original strict favorable selector; upper/lower layers are independent sets of sizes 8/7; arcs are all one-vertex deletions and the specified absent-vertex switches with exactly two neighbors in the upper set. This is a finite feasibility result only.
claims.reason: retained: the copied source replay reproduces the 15-row evidence byte for byte, and independent checks reconstruct each upper/lower layer, verify every positive arc is a legal deletion or exact two-neighbor switch, enforce each weighted node capacity, and confirm total flow equals upper supply. This retains only the finite claim; it does not prove a universal Hall statement or the primary theorem.

limitations: Only the first five stored eligible rows at each order 16, 17, and 18 were flow-tested; the other 4,976 supplied eligible rank-7 rows and all larger cases remain untested.
The census generator was not rerun; replay relies on the pinned stored result files and their row ordering.
The retained result is bounded computation and does not establish a universal weighted Hall condition or decide the lower-region ordinary aggregate.
